verdict.rationale: Alloy documents webhook authentication in which it signs the request body with a shared secret and sends the signature in the Authorization header, which lets a developer verify authenticity and payload integrity. It also documents that failed deliveries are retried on exponential backoff for 24 hours, but nothing in the evidence gives a developer a way to deduplicate those retries. missing for 10: a documented unique event/delivery ID or idempotency key for deduplicating retried notifications, details of the signature algorithm and verification steps, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can verify alert-event authenticity and deduplicate retried notifications

citations.quote: Alloy signs the request body with a shared secret and sends the signature in the Authorization header... this also verifies that the payload was not altered in transit.
Alloy webhook authentication supports multiple methods to ensure secure communication.
Subsequently, retries continue on an exponential backoff for a duration of 24 hours from the time of the first failure.
